title: English as a global language
summary: English is now a global lingua franca, for example in universities. One study says English has had a free ride on the back of global capitalism going back to the 1600s. In that century England's East India Company received its royal charter, in 1600, with a monopoly of trade in the Indian Ocean region.

uncertainty.note: The chartering of the East India Company in 1600 and early seventeenth-century transatlantic colonization mark the conventional baseline for the global dispersal of Early Modern English.

as_recorded.value: Its royal charter, granted by Queen Elizabeth I in 1600, gave it exclusive rights to trade to India and the Far East and its first trading post in India was set up at the city of Surat in 1607.
The East India Company obtained it’s royal charter in 1600 to allow it a monopoly of trade in the Indian Ocean region.
English has had a free ride on the back of global capitalism, going back as far as the 1600 s (O’Regan, 2021 )

where.modern_name: Worldwide; stand-in pin at London, United Kingdom

importance.justification: English became the most widely shared language of international exchange.

related.because: British industrial mechanization and manufacturing dominance reinforced the global commercial necessity of the English language.
